title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Civmec People
tiers.description: Directors and employees of the Group, particularly senior executives; subject to the general insider trading restrictions but not to the Closed Periods, hedging ban, short-term dealing rule or clearance procedures, which apply only to KMP.

tiers.name: KMP
tiers.description: Persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, directly or indirectly, comprising directors, senior executives and group managers, and also group corporate financial accounting personnel, executive assistants, employees and contractors notified that they are restricted persons.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; distinguished only for the identity of the clearance approver (Chairman of the Audit Committee).

tiers.name: Other directors (including Chief Executive Officer)
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chair, including the CEO; distinguished only for the identity of the clearance approver (Chair of the Board).

tiers.name: Senior executives, group manager and other restricted persons
tiers.description: KMP other than directors; distinguished only for the identity of the clearance approver (CEO).

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors and the CEO, for the purposes of the post-trade ASX Listing Rule 3.19A / SFA notification duty in section 10.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Immediate family members of Civmec People, and companies, trusts and entities controlled by them.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions or arrangement which operate to limit the economic risk of its holdings of the Company's securities

windows.start_anchor: one month prior to the release of the Company's Annual Financial Report/Half Year Financial Report to the ASX or SGX
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after the release of that report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Company's price sensitive announcements to the ASX or SGX
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after the release of that announcement

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may at its discretion vary a Closed Period rule by general announcement to all KMP, made either before or during the Closed Period; if a KMP holds undisclosed price sensitive information, they must not deal at any time regardless of any such variation.

exceptions.evidence: transfer of securities between a KMP and someone closely related to the KMP or by a KMP to their superannuation fund, in respect of which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in the trading policy;
disposal of securities arising from the acceptance of a take-over offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back;
a disposal of rights acquired under a pro rate issue;

an acquisition of securities under a security purchase plan or a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan where: (i) the KMP did not commence or amend their participation in the plan during a prohibited period; and (ii) this policy does not permit the KMP to withdraw from the plan during a prohibited period other than in exceptional circumstances;
the obtaining by a director of a share qualification;
an acquisition of securities under an employee incentive scheme;
where the Company has an employee incentive scheme with a KMP as a trustee of the scheme, an acquisition of securities by the KMP in his or her capacity as a trustee of the scheme;

an acquisition or disposal of securities under a pre-determined investment or divestment plan for which prior written clearance has been provided ... where: (iii) the KMP did not enter into or amend the plan during a prohibited period; (iv) the plan does not permit the KMP to exercise any discretion over how, when, or whether to acquire or dispose of securities

indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of a KMP dealing in securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party, that happens to hold as part of its portfolio securities in the Company;

where this policy permits KMP to enter into a margin lending or other secured financial arrangement in relation to the Company's securities, an involuntary disposal of securities that results from the margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement.
The sale of the Company's securities is necessary to alleviate severe personal financial hardship;
The KMP has entered into a binding commitment prior to the Company being in a Closed Period where it was not reasonably foreseeable at the time the commitment would extend into a Closed Period;

The KMP is required by a court order, or there are court enforceable undertakings to transfer or sell the securities of the Company or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for them to do so; or

exceptions.approver: Board (or Chairman of the Audit Committee in respect of a trade by the Chairman)
exceptions.evidence: There are other circumstances which have not been identified in this policy, that are deemed exceptional by the Board (or by the Chairman of the Audit Committee in respect of any trade by the Chairman) and the proposed sale or disposal of the relevant securities is the only reasonably course of action available.

exemption_authority: The Board may grant written approval for a KMP to deal, including during a Closed Period, in cases of severe personal financial hardship, a pre-existing binding commitment that unexpectedly extends into a Closed Period, a court order or overriding legal/regulatory requirement, or any other circumstance the Board (or, for the Chairman, the Chairman of the Audit Committee) deems exceptional and where the proposed sale is the only reasonable course of action. Clearance decisions generally are at the Company's absolute discretion, given or refused without reasons, and a refusal must be kept confidential by the KMP.
jurisdiction_overlays: Singapore - Securities and Futures Act (Cap. 289), including SGX notification under sections 133, 137N and 137Y

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP and its Associates must not enter into transactions or arrangement which operate to limit the economic risk of its holdings of the Company's securities at any time
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This bans a put/call collar for KMP (and their Associates) in any vesting state, reinforced by the section 206J statutory prohibition for unvested or holding-locked incentive remuneration.

bespoke_clauses.clause: no dealing in unvested securities (including hedging unvested securities) is permitted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Separately from the hedging ban, KMP cannot deal at all in unvested securities, foreclosing any collar or loan over unvested incentive awards regardless of clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: where this policy permits KMP to enter into a margin lending or other secured financial arrangement in relation to the Company's securities, an involuntary disposal of securities that results from the margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement [is excluded from the policy's restrictions]
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy assumes KMP can be permitted to enter secured financing but never states the conditions for that permission elsewhere; the bank should have the Company confirm the applicable clearance process before relying on the loan leg being available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: an involuntary disposal of securities that results from the margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a compliant secured loan were in place, the lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the policy's restrictions (including Closed Periods), giving certainty for lender enforcement timing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If approval to trade Company securities is refused, the KMP seeking the approval must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A refused clearance for any permissible leg cannot be disclosed to the bank, limiting transparency in structuring discussions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If written clearance is granted, it is only valid for a period of one week after notification of approval ... Written clearance is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of inside information prior to trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any cleared step in structuring must be completed within one week (or a specified alternative period) and is automatically voided if inside information arises before execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy also extends (in certain respects) to the immediate family members of Civmec People, and to companies, trusts and entities controlled by them ("Associates"). ... KMP and its Associates must not enter into transactions or arrangement which operate to limit the economic risk
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family member, trust or controlled entity does not escape the hedging ban or Closed Period restrictions.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar cannot be implemented for KMP under this policy: section 7.1 bans KMP and their Associates from any transaction that limits the economic risk of their Company shareholding 'at any time', squarely catching a purchased put and written call collar, and section 6.1 separately and more broadly prohibits KMP from any dealing at all, not just hedging, in unvested securities. These bans apply without a stated clearance route and are reinforced by the section 206J statutory prohibition on unvested or holding-locked incentive remuneration. The loan leg is more ambiguous: clause 11.1(j) assumes 'this policy permits KMP to enter into a margin lending or other secured financial arrangement' and excludes a lender's resulting involuntary sale from the policy's restrictions, but no other provision sets out the terms on which such an arrangement is actually permitted, so the bank should have the Company confirm the applicable clearance process (most likely the general section 9 pre-clearance procedure) before assuming the loan leg is available. Even where a step is otherwise permissible, KMP need written clearance from the Chair of the Board, another director, or the CEO (as applicable) at least 48 hours in advance, valid for only one week and automatically void on receipt of inside information, and cannot deal during the Closed Periods absent Board-approved exceptional circumstances. Overall, this policy forecloses the collar's option legs outright for KMP, and the loan leg's availability turns on resolving an internal drafting gap with the Company before it can be relied upon.
